articles.title: Oil prices fall as traders assess Russian diesel supply prospects and Saudi-Houthi conflict
articles.summary: Oil prices fell Tuesday as investors weighed prospects of more Russian energy entering global markets, while concerns over the Saudi-Houthi conflict limited losses. articles.title: IMF warns bond yields could see a 'disorderly' spike as debt, inflation risks worsen
articles.summary: BANGKOK – The International Monetary Fund warned Tuesday that government bond yields could rise in a disorderly fashion, as rising inflation, mounting debt and AI-related borrowings pressure sovereign bond markets. Government bond yields in several advanced economies have climbed to multidecade highs, driven by higher energy costs due to the Middle East conflict and expectations for tighter monetary conditions as central banks look to curb resurgent inflation.

articles.title: SK Hynix, SoftBank shares plunge as tech stocks in Asia track Wall Street chip sell-off
articles.summary: semiconductor shares spilled into regional markets, with worries over artificial intelligence financing and intensifying competition denting sentiment. Shares of South Korean chip giant SK Hynix, a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial intelligence applications, plunged more than 8%, while rival Samsung Electronics shed 7.9% — both hit their lowest intra-day levels since August.

articles.title: Six Flags shares plunge after-hours following report of deadly roller coaster incident
articles.summary: Shares of Six Flags Entertainment plunged more than 10% in after-hours trading Monday following reports of a deadly roller coaster incident at one of its amusement parks in Georgia, marking a sharp reversal from gains during the regular session. The stock had closed 4.5% higher during regular trading before the after-hours sell-off. The company's shares have fallen 22% year to date.

articles.title: 'Boring is not bad': CEO of Southeast Asia's largest bank pitches Singapore as a haven amid global turmoil
articles.summary: SINGAPORE — Southeast Asia's biggest bank by assets is making a pitch to investors that Singapore and its businesses can help them navigate many of the uncertainties around the globe. "In this huge time of volatility, 'boring' is not bad, right?" The investing and business climate worldwide has been upended by everything from trade wars and El Niño-related weather issues to the Iran conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says the bull market's remarkable 4-year run offers a crucial lesson for investors
articles.summary: The stock market has given investors plenty of reasons to sell over the past four years. The rally began amid widespread pessimism about inflation and the economy, yet none of those setbacks managed to derail it. A $10,000 investment in Meta Platforms would have grown to more than $58,800 as shares climbed 488%.

articles.title: IonQ to acquire cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal for up to $1.3 billion
articles.summary: Quantum computing platform IonQ said on Monday it will acquire cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in performance-based earnouts. The move is designed to defend against and uncover attackers targeting generative artificial intelligence large-language models and AI agents, and to protect against emerging quantum threats, the companies said in a press release.

articles.title: A massive trade just happened in surging shares of Snap
articles.summary: Don't call it a comeback yet, but shares of beleaguered social media stock Snap Inc. Snap shares have traded under $10 since July 2025 following a near-complete collapse from over $80 at the stock's high in 2021 to a low of $3.81 in April. But now, as excitement swirls over social media giant Meta Platforms' AI agent, traders are pouring into Snap call options on Monday, propelling trading volume to more than four times the month-long average, Cboe LiveVol data show.

articles.title: The bull market turned 4 years old on Monday. Investors say reaching a fifth birthday could be challenging
articles.summary: Since the release of ChatGPT in late 2022, investors have hungered for all things related to the AI trade, with the stocks most tied to the build-out — the so-called "picks and shovels" — flying to whole new stratospheres because of the technology. After such an extraordinary run, investors wonder how much longer the rally can continue, especially as they face ongoing fears around higher inflation, surging bond yields and a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

articles.title: Why older Americans' wealth may be helping keep consumer spending strong
articles.summary: Economists have debated whether we're still in a "K-shaped economy" — where higher-income households' spending masks financial strain among lower- and middle-income Americans. Consumer spending resilience may be better explained by generations than by income differences, said economist Ed Yardeni, president and chief investment strategist of Yardeni Research. He calls it a "G-shaped economy" because it illustrates a generational divide.

articles.title: UnitedHealth shares are doing something unusual ahead of earnings
articles.summary: The only thing more expensive than health insurance is perhaps the costs of insuring shares of health insurers. In other words, options prices - the cost of insuring the underlying stock - are expensive, which sets up well for short premium strategies. In the case of UnitedHealth shares, traders can sell November premium to cut the cost of a longer-dated January call by more than half.
